definitions: someone's age or the time that someone lives or has lived :
examples: Rachel and I have been going there for years.
I've been meaning to clean out the garage for years.
I haven't seen my uncle in years.
She hadn't thought about him in years.
It's years since I've been swimming .
It's been years since I laughed so much.

definitions: having lived or existed for only a short time and not old :
used after someone's name to show that they are the younger of two people who have the same name , especially a father and son :
to look younger than you really are:
young people considered together as a group :
examples: Young people nowadays are under so much pressure .
The trees in this part of the forest are still fairly young.
Philippa is the youngest person in the family .
Angela is two years younger than Clare.

definitions: used when the subject of the verb is "you" or the person being spoken to, and the object is the same person :
used for emphasis when the subject is "you":
to behave in your usual manner , rather than behaving in a way you think other people might like:
alone or without help from anyone else :
examples: Be careful with that knife or you'll cut yourself!
Did you make the dress yourself?
The best thing you can do is to go into the interview and just be yourself.
I'm amazed you managed to move those boxes all by yourself.
